subject.title: [Feature]: Make Skill Workshop extensible for custom skill creation workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated skill-creation authority/pre-selection API for custom workflows before `skill_workshop`, or keep the current Skill Workshop-first routing plus existing tool policy surfaces?
rationale: The requested change would define new product and plugin API semantics around who owns skill creation, when core tool routing yields to custom workflows, and whether any new config can disable direct workshop use.

options.title: Design a narrow authority seam
options.body: Add a small plugin/runtime contract that lets an enabled custom workflow prepare proposal content before Skill Workshop persists it, while keeping Skill Workshop as the only write boundary.

options.title: Use existing policy surfaces
options.body: Document `tools.allow`/`tools.deny`, optional plugin tools, and `/learn` as the supported customization path, accepting that model routing will not have a first-class custom authority guarantee.

options.title: Defer to meta-skill work
options.body: Wait for the broader meta-skill orchestration direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89959 before deciding whether this needs a separate API.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authority seam
recommendation.body: Add a small plugin/runtime contract that lets an enabled custom workflow prepare proposal content before Skill Workshop persists it, while keeping Skill Workshop as the only write boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Skill Workshop prompt, diagnostics, and skill-suggestion work makes this handle the clearest current routing/product owner candidate among the history signals.
